Subject: Production readiness notes and technical next steps (Ridgefield)

Hi Alex / Tara —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the concrete next steps so we don’t lose momentum. I tried to keep this tight and action-oriented.

Key pain & goals we heard
- Real-time claim summarization at ~150 requests/sec peak, P95 latency goal <= 150ms per request (prefers sub-100ms for UI interactions).
- Strong data isolation requirements — patient PHI processed in private deployment behind their VPC and customer-managed KMS.
- Quality: existing model truncated clinical context at times; they want consistent hallucination behavior and a quick regression guard when we change models.

Technical constraints Alex confirmed
- Avg prompt length: ~1.2k tokens; worst-case multi-section payloads up to 6k tokens (pre-processed).
- Burst pattern: 10x baseline for short windows during end-of-day batch processing.
- Must provide audit logs (per-request trace IDs) and retention settings of 90 days.

Proposed Redwood approach (brief)
- Private deployment (VPC) with dedicated capacity pools for Ridgefield (predictable throughput + KMS integration).
- Split routing: low-latency UI traffic to quantized local model variant; high-context batch jobs to larger model variant with cached KV sequences.
- KV caching + prefix caching for repeated patient prompts to reduce cost and meet latency SLOs.

Immediate next steps (owners & timing)
1) Technical deep-dive with Ridgefield infra + our SRE + Marissa (solutions eng) — target Wed 11/10, 10:00am PT. (Action: Sean to send calendar invite)
2) Ridgefield to share SOC2 and example event/usage distribution (Action: Alex) — please include sample payload sizes.
3) Redwood to deliver preliminary ops estimate and draft SLA (Action: Ben) by EOD 11/10.
4) Marissa to prepare a short runbook covering KV-cache behavior, expected batching gains, and fallback routing options (Action: Marissa) by the deep-dive.

Attachments: redwood-prod-readiness-notes.pdf (ops sketch), redwood-ops-estimate.xlsx (placeholder estimate).

If anything above is incorrect or missing, flag it — otherwise we’ll proceed with scheduling and prep.

Thanks,

Thanks Sean — this looks accurate and helpful. A few clarifications: 

- The 150ms P95 is our ideal for interactive triage flows; for background batch summarization a P95 of ~500ms is acceptable if throughput is higher.
- Our worst-case 6k token payloads are after concatenating 3 prior notes + full claim text; we can pre-truncate but would prefer the engine to support full context if possible.
- Compliance note: we need per-request correlation ids surfaced back in the response header (not just in logs).

We’ll upload the SOC2 doc and a small sample of payloads to the shared folder by EOD today. Attaching the SOC2 snapshot for now: ridgefield-soc2.pdf.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Production readiness notes and technical next steps (Ridgefield) — technical prep

Alex / team —

Thanks for the SOC2 snapshot, Alex. I pulled together a short technical sketch ahead of tomorrow’s deep-dive so we can use it as the working doc. Main bullets below; I’ll bring diagrams to the call.

1) Latency & throughput plan\- Low-latency UI route:
  - Model: 7B quantized variant serving in the VPC (int8/float16 depending on GPU), optimized for low-hopping attention.
  - Target: P95 <= 120ms for 1.2k token avg (measured from API gateway ingress to first-token streamed).
  - Batching: small continuous batching with max batch window 12ms; prefer request coalescing at gateway for bursts.

- High-throughput batch route:
  - Model: 70B non-quantized (or fp16) variant on dedicated pool for nightly jobs; larger context (6k) served without truncation using segmented KV caching for long histories.
  - Throughput: scale pools to handle 150rps sustained for batch windows; autoscale policy to add capacity at 200rps if queue depth exceeds threshold.

2) KV caching & prefix caching\- We will implement per-user prefix caching (cache keys tied to patient id + document hash). For typical repeated queries this yields 2–4x effective latency improvement and significant token-cost reduction. Cache TTLs can be set per-route; suggest 30m for UI, 6h for batch reuse.

3) Deployment topology options\- Option A (recommended): Private VPC control plane with a dedicated Redwood capacity pool behind Ridgefield’s private subnet. KMS integration for envelope keys; egress-only endpoints for audit log shipping to Ridgefield S3.
- Option B: Hybrid — UI traffic routed through Redwood hosted nodes (lower ops) with encrypted proxying; sensitive batch jobs kept in-customer VPC. Tradeoff: more complexity in routing, easier failover with hosted nodes.

4) Model & quality controls\- Maintain stable model variants per route; implement evaluation hooks (prompt set checks) and automatic regression alerts. We’ll version pin in the deployment manifest; rollbacks via canary policy.

5) Fallbacks & graceful degradation\- On capacity constraint, fallback to smaller quantized variant with a visible rate-limited degradation path; we’ll expose a header indicating which model handled the request.

Open questions for the deep-dive
- Do you have a hard ceiling for egress to any third-party endpoints (for log shipping)?
- Expected concurrency per tenant (UI vs batch) during normal business hours?
- Any additional compliance artifacts beyond SOC2 we should prep for the deep-dive?

I’ll bring an ops-estimate and a short runbook to the call. Ben — I’ve put placeholder numbers in redwood-ops-estimate.xlsx; please refine before EOD.

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
